# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

**All three were found in a REAL shopping run tonight, not in review.** Warwick lived through every one.

> ### ⛔ AMENDMENT 1 — 2026-08-10, Larry. READ THIS BEFORE THE ACs BELOW.
>
> **Keel REFUSED the first issue of this order and was right to.** Its read-back is the authority for what follows; where this amendment and the original AC text disagree, **this amendment wins.**
>
> **The base was wrong.** The order named `0731a94`. That is PR #103's merge commit and `main` is **87 commits ahead of it**, so *every* line number and symbol the ACs cite is absent from the declared base. `git grep clarification_deferred` at `0731a94` returns nothing at all.
>
> **The corrected base is local `main` at `9424f06`.** Every site below was verified present there. `9424f06` differs from `75caa25` only by `tools/governor/**` (an unrelated permission-guard fix) — no `services/**` byte moved, so the citations hold exactly.
>
> **`origin/main` is `6eaf0dc` and is NOT an ancestor of local `main`.** Tonight's work is local plus the safety branch `backup/2026-08-10-local-main-safety`. Larry owns that lifecycle; it is stated so you are not surprised by it.
>
> **AC1 is now a NARROWER question than it was, because half of it landed while the order was being written.** See AC1 as amended.
>
> **AC2's stated cause was FALSIFIED by your read-back and is withdrawn.** See AC2 as amended.
>
> **AC3 stands exactly as written.** You already confirmed the three sites are real. **Build it first** — it is the one unambiguous fix and Warwick is asleep waiting on a working runtime.

**AC1 — the notification storm. `clarification_deferred` re-queues every pass.**
Site: `runPipeline.js` ~line 803, `key: outboxKeyFor(shop.shop_ref, \`clarification_deferred.${held.question_key}\`)`.
**The observed keys prove the cause:** `...clarification_deferred.q8f8d3866#7`, `#9`, `#13`, `#17`, `#20`. **`held.question_key` carries an incrementing ROUND SUFFIX**, so the idempotency key never matches itself and "one notice per question" became **one notice per pass — ~20 cards between 23:30 and 00:05.**
Fix: key the notice on something **stable for the life of the question** — the base key with the round suffix stripped, or the parent question key. **The comment above it already promises this behaviour; make the code keep the promise.**

> **AC1 AS AMENDED — 2026-08-10, Larry.** You established that `65efb94` and `47b5de8` landed a partial fix at 01:13 while this order was being written: the enqueue is now guarded by `spentLedgerGenerations(noticeFamily) === 0`, and the false comment is already corrected. **Do not re-implement that.**
>
> **What remains is the half you identified, and it is now the whole of AC1:** the key at `runPipeline.js:814` still embeds `held.question_key` *with its round suffix*, so the **family itself moves when the round increments** — which is exactly the `#7 #9 #13 #17 #20` progression Warwick received. A generation guard that is asked about a *different family each round* cannot suppress anything.
>
> **Establish first, then fix.** The open question you named — *does `question_round` advance on the deferred path?* — is answerable from the code and the durable events, and answering it is part of AC1. **If it advances, the family is unstable and you close it.** If it provably cannot advance, say so with the evidence and AC1 is discharged as already-fixed; that is a legitimate outcome, not a failure to deliver.
>
> **The acceptance property is unchanged and it is the real one:** a test that reproduces **twenty cards from one held question across many passes**, red before and green after. A test that only asserts the generation guard fires is the mistake this defect already made once.

**AC2 — an answer becomes a spurious shop.**
Warwick typed a bare (non-reply) message answering the open question. The answer router **correctly** mapped it — `runtime.js` ~line 295, the "NOTHING TO CHOOSE BETWEEN" branch that maps a bare message when exactly one question is open. **And `pollIntake` ALSO ingested it as a new shopping list**, creating `SHOP-2026-08-10` whose single line reads *"any gloves, i don't care want to rotate as soon as safe to do so!"*.
`runtime.js:924` already excludes `msg.reply_to_message`, so **replies are safe — bare messages are not.** The two paths do not coordinate.
Fix: **a message consumed as an answer must not also be ingested as a list.** One message, one meaning.

> **AC2 AS AMENDED — 2026-08-10, Larry. The stated cause above is WITHDRAWN.**
>
> You proved it false: the two paths **do** coordinate. `runOnce` reads open questions, builds a `claim`, passes it to `pollIntake`, which hands it to `shopperIntake.runIntake`; `shopperIntake.js:702` calls it **before** `buildRecord`, and `shopperIntake.test.js:633` already asserts the exact symptom must not happen. The seam exists, is tested, and is wired in production via `routeAsdairUpdate` (`runtime.js:1168`).
>
> **So the seam RAN AND FAILED ANYWAY, and that — not building a seam — is AC2.** `SHOP-2026-08-10` exists in the household database with one line reading *"any gloves, i don't care want to rotate as soon as safe to do so!"*. Something real defeated a mechanism that a green test says works. **A passing test over a failing production path is the most valuable thing in this order** — it means the test asserts a different situation than the one Warwick hit.
>
> **Deliverable: establish the actual cause, then fix it, then make the test reproduce the PRODUCTION situation rather than the imagined one.** Candidate directions, not a prescription: the claim may be empty or stale at the moment of the fetch (built before the question existed, or after it closed); the update may arrive on a path that never carries the claim; the message may be fetched in a pass where no question was yet open and only *later* routed as an answer; `runIntake` may receive the claim but not match on it (id shape, round suffix, normalisation).
>
> **If the true cause turns out to be a race rather than a logic error, say so plainly and fix it as one** — an ordering defect fixed as if it were a matching defect will come back.
>
> **The file surface is widened to `services/asdair/intake/**` and `services/asdair/bot/**` for exactly this.** If the cause still lands outside all three, stop and report rather than reaching.

**AC3 — a cosmetic acknowledgement failure kills the pass.**
Sites: `runtime.js` ~lines 495, 503, 510 — `await bot.answerTap(...)` **unguarded**. Telegram rejects a stale callback query with *"query is too old"*, the throw escapes, and **the whole pass aborts** (`pass_failed`, repeatedly, all evening).
**The tap itself is already durable** — every answer landed despite this. So the failure is purely the visual acknowledgement, and it must never abort pipeline work.
Fix: guard each `answerTap`; log and continue. **Do not "fix" it by removing the acknowledgement** — the missing confirmation is a real UX defect and Warwick tapped repeatedly because of it. Record that separately.

**AC4 — mutation-demonstrate all three.** Each test must fail on the pre-fix behaviour and pass after. **Verify each mutation actually applied (`git diff` non-empty) before trusting a red or green** — an unapplied mutation looks exactly like a passing one.
